- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast periods.  
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes in sentiment or price, particularly if sentiment turns negative mid-period.  
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–15% if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days after peak.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 85% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5–7 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.  
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in 3–5 consecutive days, apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment magnitude.
